case_name: Gopal Lal vs State Of Rajasthan
facts_of_case: After falling out with his wife Kanchan, Gopal Lal contracted a second marriage with Gopi in 1969. His first wife filed a complaint and he was convicted of bigamy under section 494 I.P.C. He appealed to the Supreme Court.

legal_principles.principle: The second marriage will become void only because of the provisions of section 17 of the Hindu Marriage Act.
legal_principles.held: Therefore, the contention that the second marriage being void section 494 I.P.C. will have no application is not correct.
cited_cases: Gopal Lal vs State Of Rajasthan, (1979) X SCC Y

Bhaurao Shankar Lokhande and Anr. v. State of Maharashtra and Ors., [1965]2 S.C.R. 837; Kanwal Ram and Ors. v. The Himachal Pradesh Administration, [1966]1 S.C.R. 539 and Priya Bala Ghosh v. Suresh Chandra Ghosh; [1973]3 S.C.R. 961
legal_principles.significance: HIGH — for understanding the application of section 494 I.P.C.

legal_principles.principle: The essential ingredients of section 494 are: (1) that the accused spouse must have contracted the first marriage, and (2) that while the first marriage was subsisting, the accused spouse contracted a second marriage.

outcome.final_order: The appellant must be held to have committed the offence of Bigamy as contemplated by section 494 I.P.C.
